content:
maria: Hey folks — FinServX POC needs a private deployment connectivity spec. They want: 1) site-to-site VPN to our private control plane, 2) egress via their on-prem proxy (BYO egress), and 3) static allowlist for healthchecks. Can eng confirm IPs/ports and any caveats?

dan: Quick Q — does their VPN SNAT? If they SNAT to a small set of public IPs we can use those for allowlisting. Also is the VPN static routes or BGP?

maria: They SNAT to two static egress IPs (203.0.113.45 and 203.0.113.46). VPN will be static routes for the POC. They will only permit outbound 443.

kevin: For Private deployments our control plane/agent comms are TLS (443) by default. Healthchecks also happen over TLS from a small pool of IPs. Typical firewall snippet we hand out: 

ALLOW TCP 203.0.113.45:443 -> 198.51.100.10:443  # customer egress -> redwood endpoint
ALLOW TCP 203.0.113.46:443 -> 198.51.100.10:443
ALLOW TCP 198.51.100.20:443 -> CUSTOMER_AGENT_PORT  # control-plane healthchecks

Replace the 198.51.100.* with our published list.

maria: Customer asked whether TCP idle timeouts will break streaming inference sessions. Their firewall idle timeout is 90s.

alex: Streaming sessions can be interrupted by idle timeouts. Options: (a) application-level heartbeats (we recommend 30s), (b) use an intermediate proxy with long idle timeout, or (c) use Redwood-managed proxy (not applicable here if they insist on BYO). We'll note heartbeat in runbook.

pete: On security: we support customer KMS for keys and can forward audit logs to their SIEM. Need to confirm if they require mutual TLS on the control channel or just client cert validation. Also call out TLS inspection (MITM) impact on cert pinning and function-calling.

infra-bot: KB: Private deploy connectivity checklist -> https://docs.redwood.ai/private/connectivity :pushpin:

dan: Pricing check for sales: if they route egress through their on-prem proxy (BYO egress), do we bill outbound bandwidth?

kevin: If egress stays on the customer's network (BYO egress) we do not bill their outbound bandwidth. If they use Redwood-managed egress/NAT or proxy we charge egress as a separate line item. Finance approves exceptions for very high volumes.

maria: Sales needs an official allowlist and a 1-page POC runbook (ports, recommended heartbeat, symptoms to look for, sample tcpdump). Can eng produce these before the tech call tomorrow 10:00am?

alex: I'll produce the allowlist with concrete IPs and a short runbook. Checklist for the call: - confirm their NAT pair (we have 203.0.113.45/46) - confirm static route parameters and pre-shared key - confirm whether they will perform TLS inspection - agree on heartbeat interval (we recommend 30s)

dan: Note for static-route VPNs: ensure healthchecks originate consistently from the same IPs (/32) otherwise stateful firewalls may drop replies. I'll add that note to the runbook.

pete: I'll draft answers for security questionnaire items: egress logging, KMS integration, cipher suites (TLS1.2+ modern ciphers), and SLA differences if they choose BYO egress vs Redwood-managed.

kevin: I'll upload the standard firewall sample and pricing blurb to the shared drive after the call.

maria: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: — scheduling tech call now, expecting final doc after the 10am sync.
